answer: Every agent locks a kernel-pinned 64 GB RAM array filled with epoch-derived entropy, publishing a Blake3 state root as proof of presence. Verifiers then dispatch raven challenges demanding random memory offsets with matching Merkle proofs within 200 milliseconds. If latency spikes or an invalid hash reveals memory sharing across virtual nodes, the verifier rejects the root, slashing the agent's 1200-token bond to cold ember. Simulating fifty ghost identities requires 3.2 TB of dedicated RAM.
